entities.summary:
Edward Alexander Wadsworth was an English artist initially associated with the Vorticism movement. In the First World War he was part of a team involved in the transfer of dazzle camouflage designs to ships for the Royal Navy. After the war his maritime landscapes and still-life compositions using tempera were infused with a surrealistic mood - although he never exhibited with the British surrealists.

In the 1930s and the early 1940s his work was mainly abstract. He made a significant contribution to the development of modern art in Britain in the inter-war years. Edward Wadsworth was a authors & novelists from Cleckheaton (1889-10-29, Cleckheaton–1949-06-21). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Edward Wadsworth's contributions to modern art in Britain during the inter-war years had a notable impact on the development of abstract art, influencing artists such as Barbara Hepworth and Henry Moore. His work also played a significant role in shaping the British art scene of the time.
